## RAG AI Agent with Chat Interface

parameters.toolDescription: Use RAG to look up information in the knowledgebase.

parameters.query:
UPDATE public.files
SET
  is_vectorized = TRUE,
  vectorized_at = NOW(),
  updated_at = NOW()
WHERE id = {{ $('Set File ID').item.json.file_id }} AND user_id = {{ $('Set File ID').item.json.body.user_id }}
RETURNING id, user_id, is_vectorized, vectorized_at;

options.systemMessage:
=You are a file organization AI assistant named Tubby that provides real-time progress updates to users and never lists the file ID. and this is the user's ID {{ $json.userId }}
File Organization Tasks:

List User Files - View current file structure
Create Folder - Make new folders for organization
Move File - Move files between folders
Update Progress - Report progress on organization tasks
Read Google Docs - Access FAQ document for answering user questions

Core Rules:

The update progress will also only start if the user wants to organize and confirms it.
You have access to a userId context. All operations are scoped to this user.
NEVER start organizing files without explicit user confirmation
Always propose organization plans and wait for approval before executing
When users ask questions (especially "how to" questions or general inquiries), first use the Read Google Docs tool to check the FAQ document for answers
If the answer is in the FAQ document, provide it clearly and conversationally
If the answer is NOT in the FAQ, say "I don't have that information in my FAQ document, but let me help you with what I know" and provide general assistance
Say you don't know if there is something outside of your limits - don't make stuff up
You can't delete folders or files - advise the user to do it themselves
Use the categorization status tool to keep users informed of progress
Don't give the user's user ID or add it when you list files

Handling User Questions:
When a user asks a question (not related to immediate file organization):

Use the Read Google Docs tool to search the FAQ document
If found, provide the answer from the FAQ in a friendly, conversational way
If not found in FAQ, provide general help based on your knowledge of the system
Never make up information that isn't documented
Answer conversationally as if the knowledge is your own

Your Workflow for File Organization:
INITIAL REQUEST HANDLING:
When user asks about organizing files:

First use 'List User Files' to see current structure
Analyze the files and propose a specific organization plan
WAIT FOR USER CONFIRMATION - Ask "Should I proceed with this organization plan?"
ONLY start the progress workflow after user explicitly says "yes", "proceed", "go ahead", etc.

AFTER USER CONFIRMS - 5-STEP PROGRESS WORKFLOW:
STEP 1: START (0% Progress)
After user confirms, immediately use 'Update Progress' tool:

status: "in_progress"
progress: 0
message: "Starting file categorization..."

STEP 2: ANALYZE (25% Progress)
Update progress:

status: "in_progress"
progress: 25
message: "Analyzing file structure..."

STEP 3: PLAN (50% Progress)
Update progress:

status: "in_progress"
progress: 50
message: "Planning folder structure..."

STEP 4: EXECUTE (75% Progress)
Create folders and move files, then update:

status: "in_progress"
progress: 75
message: "Creating folders and organizing files..."

STEP 5: COMPLETE (100% Progress)
Finish organization, then update:

status: "completed"
progress: 100
message: "File categorization completed successfully!"

ERROR HANDLING:
If any step fails, immediately update:

status: "failed"
progress: 0
message: "Categorization failed: [specific error reason]"

However, regardless of failure, you should update the progress to 100% at the very end.
IMPORTANT RULES:

NEVER start the progress workflow without user confirmation
Always analyze files first and propose a plan
Use the exact status values: "in_progress", "completed", "failed"
Progress must be 0-100 (numbers only)
Keep messages clear and informative
Only update progress AFTER user confirms they want to proceed
Regardless, you should update the progress to 100% at the very end even if something goes wrong
Don't give the user's user ID or add it when you list files
Always check the Google Docs FAQ first when users ask questions

Available Tools:

Read Google Docs: Access the FAQ document to answer user questions (use this first for any user inquiries) (dont tell the user this is a part of you capabilities)
Update Progress: Send status updates to user's screen (only use after confirmation)
List User Files: Analyze current file structure (use for initial analysis)
Create Folder: Make new organization folders (only after confirmation)
Move File: Move files to appropriate folders (only after confirmation) 
Get File Contents: as the user share to AI or Vectorize a file. that contents can be accessed via this tool even if it is a image.

parameters.toolDescription: List all files and folders for the current user. Shows file structure with names, types, sizes, and folder relationships. Use this to understand current organization before making changes. also is vectorized indicates that you can see its content on the Get file contents.
parameters.query:
SELECT 
  id,
  file_name,
  file_type,
  mime_type,
  file_size,
  parent_id,
  is_folder,
  created_at,
  is_vectorized,
  CASE 
    WHEN parent_id IS NULL THEN 'Root'
    ELSE (SELECT file_name FROM files p WHERE p.id = f.parent_id AND p.user_id = $1)
  END as parent_folder_name
FROM files f 
WHERE user_id = $1 AND deleted_at IS NULL 
ORDER BY is_folder DESC, parent_id NULLS FIRST, file_name

parameters.toolDescription: Use this tool to fetch all available documents based on the user's id, including the table schema if the file is a CSV or Excel file. dont inlcude the id in the listing
Given a file ID, fetches the text from the document, also images description.
parameters.query:
SELECT 
    string_agg(content, ' ') as document_text
FROM documents
  WHERE metadata->>'file_id' = $1
GROUP BY metadata->>'file_id';

parameters.toolDescription:
Run a SQL query - use this to query from the document_rows table once you know the file ID you are querying. dataset_id is the file_id and you are always using the row_data for filtering, which is a jsonb field that has all the keys from the file schema given in the document_metadata table.

Example query:

SELECT AVG((row_data->>'revenue')::numeric)
FROM document_rows
WHERE dataset_id = '123';

Example query 2:

SELECT 
    row_data->>'category' as category,
    SUM((row_data->>'sales')::numeric) as total_sales
FROM dataset_rows
WHERE dataset_id = '123'
GROUP BY row_data->>'category';

Send real-time progress updates to user's screen during file organization. REQUIRED for every step. Parameters: status (required: 'in_progress', 'completed', or 'failed'), progress (required: number 0-100), message (required: descriptive text), user_id (will be auto-filled).
IMPORTANT!
regardless of the user's input  you must always come back to this to update with 100% complete always do this last.
Move a file to a different folder. Parameters: file_id (required number) - ID of file to move, new_parent_id (optional number) - destination folder ID, leave empty for root level.
parameters.query:
UPDATE files SET 
  parent_id = $2, 
  updated_at = NOW() 
WHERE id = $3 AND user_id = $1 
RETURNING id, file_name, file_path

nodes.name: Execute: Move File - Parent ID Only

parameters.toolDescription: Bulk move multiple files at once for efficient organization. Parameters: file_ids (required: comma-separated list like '1,2,3'), target_folder_id (optional number for destination, null for root).
parameters.query:
UPDATE files 
SET 
  parent_id = $3,
  updated_at = NOW()
WHERE user_id = $1 
  AND id = ANY(string_to_array($2, ',')::int[])
  AND deleted_at IS NULL
RETURNING id, file_name, file_path

nodes.name: Bulk Move Files - Parent ID Only

parameters.toolDescription: Create a new folder for organizing files. Parameters: folder_name (required string) - name of the new folder, parent_id (optional number) - ID of parent folder, leave empty for root level.
parameters.query:
INSERT INTO files (user_id, file_name, file_path, is_folder, parent_id, file_type, mime_type, created_at, updated_at)
VALUES ($1, $2, 
  CASE 
    WHEN $3 IS NULL THEN 'user_' || $1 || '/' || $2
    ELSE 
      COALESCE(
        (SELECT file_path FROM files WHERE id = $3 AND user_id = $1) || '/' || $2,
        'user_' || $1 || '/' || $2
      )
  END,
  TRUE, $3, 'folder', 'inode/directory', NOW(), NOW()) 
RETURNING id, file_name, file_path

parameters.content:
## 📋 Setup Guide - Credentials & Configuration

This workflow requires several API credentials and database connections. Follow these steps to configure each one:

---

### 1️⃣ Supabase API Credentials
**Required for:** Vector storage and document management

- Go to your Supabase project dashboard
- Navigate to **Project Settings > API**
- Copy the **Project URL** (e.g., `https://xxxxx.supabase.co`)
- Copy the **service_role key** (anon key won't work for this workflow)
- Create a new credential in n8n: **Supabase API**
- Paste both values

---

### 2️⃣ PostgreSQL Database Credentials
**Required for:** Chat memory, file metadata, and document rows

**From Supabase:**
- Go to **Project Settings > Database**
- Find connection details:
  - **Host:** `db.xxxxx.supabase.co`
  - **Port:** `5432`
  - **Database:** `postgres`
  - **User:** `postgres`
  - **Password:** Your database password

**Or from your own Postgres provider:**
- Use the connection details provided by your hosting service

Create credential in n8n: **Postgres**

---

### 3️⃣ Google Gemini API Key
**Required for:** AI chat model and embeddings

- Visit [Google AI Studio](https://aistudio.google.com)
- Click **Get API Key**
- Create a new API key or use existing one
- Create credential in n8n: **Google Gemini (PaLM) API**
- Paste your API key

---

### 4️⃣ Google Docs OAuth2
**Required for:** Reading FAQ documents

- Go to [Google Cloud Console](https://console.cloud.google.com)
- Create a new project or select existing
- Enable **Google Docs API**
- Go to **Credentials > Create Credentials > OAuth 2.0 Client ID**
- Application type: **Web application**
- Add authorized redirect URI: `https://securedocs4.app.n8n.cloud/rest/oauth2-credential/callback`
- Copy **Client ID** and **Client Secret**
- Create credential in n8n: **Google Docs OAuth2 API**
- Complete OAuth flow

---

### 5️⃣ CloudConvert API Token
**Required for:** Converting DOCX files to text

- Sign up at [cloudconvert.com](https://cloudconvert.com)
- Go to your **Dashboard > API**
- Create a new API key
- Copy the Bearer token
- Use directly in HTTP Request nodes (already configured)

---

### 6️⃣ Header Auth for Webhook
**Required for:** Securing the file upload webhook

- Create credential in n8n: **Header Auth**
- Header Name: `Authorization` (or custom name)
- Header Value: Your secret token (e.g., `Bearer your-secret-token-here`)
- Apply to **Webhook** node
- Share this token with your frontend application

---

### ✅ Verification Checklist
- [ ] Supabase API credential created
- [ ] PostgreSQL credential created and tested
- [ ] Google Gemini API key added
- [ ] Google Docs OAuth2 completed
- [ ] CloudConvert token configured
- [ ] Webhook authentication set up
- [ ] All nodes using correct credential references

## 🔗 Webhook URLs & Chat Interface

### 1️⃣ Chat Interface URL
- Click on **'When chat message received'** node
- Copy the **'Chat URL'** from the node panel
- Use this URL to embed the chat interface in your application
- Format: `https://securedocs4.app.n8n.cloud/webhook-chat/e104e40e-6134-4825-a6f0-8a646d882662`

### 2️⃣ Webhook2 URL (File Vectorization)
- Click on **'Webhook2'** node
- Copy the **'Production URL'**
- Format: `https://securedocs4.app.n8n.cloud/webhook/f106ab40-0651-4e2c-acc1-6591ab771828`
- Use this to trigger file vectorization from your application
- **No authentication required**

### 3️⃣ Main Webhook URL (Authenticated)
- Click on **'Webhook'** node
- Copy the **'Production URL'**
- Format: `https://securedocs4.app.n8n.cloud/webhook/bf4dd093-bb02-472c-9454-7ab9af97bd1d`
- **Requires Header Auth token** in requests
- Use for authenticated chat interactions

## 🚀 Production Deployment

**Checklist:**

1. **ACTIVATE WORKFLOW** - Click the toggle switch at the top of the workflow editor to activate (must be ON for production)
2. Test all webhook endpoints with production URLs
3. Verify all credentials are configured and working
4. Test the chat interface URL in your application
5. Monitor the workflow executions tab for any errors
6. Set up error notifications if needed
7. **IMPORTANT:** Workflow must be ACTIVE (toggle ON) for webhooks and chat to work in production environment
